title: Experiment Safety and Metric Harmonization Compact Manual
author: Asha Menon
body:
Summary

This compact manual documents a cross-cutting, reproducible approach for running runtime experiments that touch kernel scheduling, profiling, benchmarking, and production runbooks. It prescribes safety gates, harmonized metrics, and a short remediation checklist for rapid rollback. This doc is intended for runtime engineers, oncall responders, and experimentation owners running controlled changes to scheduling policies, kernel variants, or telemetry sampling.

Scope

- Applies to: any experiment that modifies kernel selection, kernel hint propagation, admission controllers, or runtime-level batching/eviction parameters in the serving runtime.
- Excludes: model parameter changes, user prompt set changes, or user-visible model content experiments (those are handled by Model QA and Product).

Goals

1. Keep production SLOs intact during experiments (95th and 99th latency, error rate, token throughput).
2. Ensure metric comparability across runs (common tags, sampling strategy).
3. Provide fast, well-documented rollback and recovery steps if safety gates fail.

Ownership and Roles

- Experiment Owner: creates experiment charter and runs the change.
- Runtime Operator: oncall engineer responsible for monitoring and rollback.
- Telemetry Owner: maintains metric instrumentation and sampling configuration.
- SRE Reviewer: approves capacity and failure-domain checks prior to canary.

Pre-experiment Checklist (must pass before enabling traffic)

1. Charter (one paragraph) posted to the experiment tracker with expected impact, duration, and rollback criteria.
2. Runbook attached with clear sign-off columns for Experiment Owner and Runtime Operator.
3. Canary plan defined: affected zones, percent traffic, duration per step.
4. Baseline snapshot collected: 24-hour sliding window for key metrics.
5. Trace sampling and live profiling configured: enable lightweight trace at 1% and high-fidelity on shadow channels.

Metric Harmonization Guidelines

- Canonical metric names (use these exactly):
  - runtime.request.latency_ms.p50, p95, p99
  - runtime.request.error_count
  - runtime.token.throughput
  - kernel.switch.count
  - kvcache.hit_rate
  - scheduler.admission.rejected_count

- Required tags/labels on every metric: environment, deployment_id, experiment_id, kernel_variant, region
- Sampling policy: production baseline sampling must remain unchanged during experiment windows. Additional high-fidelity samples should be routed to shadow channels only.

Experiment Safety Gates (automated and manual)

Automated gates (fail experiment immediately if any triggers):
- > 3x increase in runtime.request.error_count in 5-minute rolling window
- p99 latency increase > 30% vs baseline over 10 minutes
- Token throughput drop > 25% sustained for 5 minutes

Manual escalation triggers (operator decides rollback after assessment):
- p95 latency increase between 15% and 30% sustained for 10 minutes
- Kernel.switch.count spike without matching change in request load
- Unexplained increase in scheduler.admission.rejected_count

Kernel / Scheduler Impact Table (quick reference)

| Change           | Likely short-term impact           | Observability signals to watch               | Recommended canary step |
|------------------|------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|------------------------|
| batch_size_up    | lower throughput variance, higher latency for short requests | p50/p95 latency divergence; kernel.dispatch.wait_ms | 1% traffic, 5m        |
| prefetch_hint_en | improved warmstart; higher memory pressure | kvcache.hit_rate up; memory_pressure metric | 0.5% shadow, then 2%  |
| preemptive_split | reduces long-tail by interrupting heavy kernels; risk of more kernel.switch | kernel.switch.count; p99 latency | 0.1% stage, monitor 15m |
| admission_tight  | protects latency SLOs, may reject low-priority work | scheduler.admission.rejected_count; error_count | 1% canary, 10m       |

Profiling Playbook (short)

1. Baseline capture: collect 5-minute microtraces for representative routes prior to change.
2. Warm shadow profiling: route 0.5% of traffic to the experimental binary with full trace baggage.
3. Aggregation and diff: use the profiling pipeline to compare kernel-level CPU/GPU time and serialization stalls between baseline and experiment.
4. Rapid hypothesis loop: if a kernel shows +25% GPU time, pin to kernel variant A and re-run a micro-canary.

Benchmarking and Acceptance Protocol (quick runbook)

- Bench harness: use the accepted workload manifest (manifest_id: workload/production-replay/v2) with token distribution and concurrency matrix.
- Acceptance criteria: no increase in p99 latency > 20% under matched concurrency; no regression in kvcache.hit_rate < -5 percentage points; kernel errors remain zero.
- Experiment can graduate to broader canary only after 3 successful acceptance runs spaced at least 2 hours apart.

Rollback and Recovery Procedure (explicit)

1. Immediate: disable experiment toggle or revert scheduler config using the emergency toggle endpoint: curl -XPOST https://ops-api.internal/v1/exp-toggle/{experiment_id}/disable -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
2. Recompute capacity: if eviction pressure observed, run: ./ops-scripts/redistribute-shards --grace-period=60s
3. Verify: confirm p95 and p99 back to baseline within 15 minutes. If not, escalate to SRE Reviewer.

Quick Troubleshooting Decision Tree

- Symptom: p99 latency spike without error_count rise
  1) Check kernel.switch.count -> if high, consider scaling back preemptive_split.
  2) Check memory_pressure -> if high, disable prefetch_hint_en.

- Symptom: error_count spike
  1) Inspect scheduler.admission.rejected_count and recent config changes.
  2) If errors map to a single kernel variant, revert that kernel at the service control plane.

Postmortem and Data Retention

- If any automated gate fired or manual rollback was executed, an incident-lite postmortem should be produced within 48 hours. Include: baseline snapshot, experiment logs, trace samples, kernel timings, and decision rationale.
- Retain experiment traces for 90 days. Summaries and roll-forward decisions must be recorded in the experiment tracker.

Checklist for Safe Rollout Phases (canary -> ramp -> full)

1. Canary (0.1% - 1%): 30m min per step, automated gates live, operator present.
2. Ramp (1% - 10%): 1h min per step, increased trace sampling to 5% in shadow channels.
3. Full (10%+): staggered regional enablement, capacity verification with SRE, monitoring page in console set to shared view.

Appendix: Useful Commands and Probes

- Toggle an experiment: curl -XPOST https://ops-api.internal/v1/exp-toggle/{experiment_id}/(enable|disable) -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
- Collect a microtrace from node: ssh ops-node-1 -- sudo /usr/local/bin/collect-trace --pid $PID --duration 30s > /tmp/trace.json
- Quick kernel health query (PromQL): sum(rate(kernel_exec_time_ms[5m])) by (kernel_variant) / sum(rate(kernel_exec_count[5m])) by (kernel_variant)

Contacts and Escalation Path

- Oncall Runtime Operator: runtime-oncall@redwood.ai
- Telemetry Owner: telemetry@redwood.ai
- SRE escalation pager: +1-555-0101 (use for >15m unresolved SLO regressions)

End of document.
